entities.summary: Martina Sofia Helena Bergman Österberg was a Swedish-born physical education instructor and women's suffrage advocate who spent most of her working life in Britain. After studying gymnastics in Stockholm she moved to London, where she founded the first physical education instructors' college in England, to which she admitted women only. Bergman-Österberg pioneered teaching physical education as a full subject within the English school curriculum, with Swedish-style gymnastics at its core. She also advocated the wearing of gymslips by women playing sports, and played a pivotal role in the early development of netball.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Martina Bergman-Österberg's pioneering work in physical education and women's sports paved the way for the inclusion of Swedish-style gymnastics in the English school curriculum, influencing generations of students. Her advocacy led to the development of netball, a sport with over 5 million players worldwide.
